taxonomy.kew_status: Native to the Old World; introduced in North America/Texas

morphology_keys.habit: Twining or trailing vine with long branches; often prostrate on bare ground or climbing nearby vegetation.
morphology_keys.root: Deep taproot with fleshy belowground caudex.
morphology_keys.stem: Ridged, tough, essentially glabrous in local material.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate; oblong to narrowly ovate/lanceolate, with hastate or sagittate spreading basal lobes.
morphology_keys.sepals: Short, about 3–4.3 mm in Williamson County material.
morphology_keys.corolla: Broadly funnel-shaped, about 15–20 mm long and 21–30 mm across; white/cream, sometimes pinkish outside.
morphology_keys.fruit: Rounded capsule; persistent style base may form a point.

best_traits: Very short sepals compared with C. equitans

ecology.regional_note: Documented in Williamson County; included now because it is locally encountered even though introduced.

roles: 3 photos from one multi-photo Texas/Central Texas observation when available
photo_strategy.why: This should produce a more diagnostic set than choosing one random photo from five unrelated observations.
